topPRs.title: params: expose EIP-8282 system contracts for L1 library consumers
topPRs.author: joshklop
topPRs.body:
## Summary

The Optimism monorepo needs EIP-8282's canonical builder deposit/exit predeploys when generating L1 dev genesis allocations for an upstream geth subprocess. Its Go imports still resolve to op-geth, which exports the Prague queue definitions but not these two builder queues. This backport allows the consumer to use `params` consistently instead of embedding an allocation JSON fixture.

- Export `BuilderDepositAddress`, `BuilderDepositCode`, `BuilderExitAddress`, and `BuilderExitCode`, copied verbatim from [released go-ethereum v1.17.7](https://github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/blob/v1.17.7/params/protocol_params.go).
- Add canonical-address and fixed runtime-code SHA-256 regression tests.

**Library-only scope:** no changes to genesis construction, state processing, fork activation, dependencies, or generated code. This does not implement Glamsterdam in the unsupported op-geth binary. Consumer: https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/23152.

## Validation

- All four exported definitions independently compared with released upstream source.
- `go test ./params -count=1`
- `make all`
- `go run ./build/ci.go lint`
- `go run ./build/ci.go check_generate`
- `go run ./build/ci.go check_baddeps`
- `go run ./build/ci.go test` (full repository suite, including execution-spec fixtures and keeper module)
- Independent read-only Codex review: no findings in either params file. Its temporary test-submodule checkout observation was resolved by completing initialization to the unchanged pinned commits.
- Consumer queue regression test and all four Glamsterdam scenarios pass with a temporary local-module override (not committed).
